title: Nashandra
snippet: When Drangleic was ravaged by the second war with the giants and the spread of the Undead Curse, Vendrick came to realize the true nature and identity of Nashandra, and what she had coveted all along. Knowing that his time was short and that his queen had to be stopped, Vendrick created several impasses that would prevent Nashandra from seizing the throne, and sealed himself away in the Undead Crypt. This left Nashandra the sole ruler of Drangleic, albeit without much left to rule at all, as the kingdom had been all but destroyed.

title: Throne of Want
snippet:
At a certain moment during his reign, Nashandra came to Drangleic, she coveted the Throne of Want and the power of the First Flame, and seduced Vendrick in order to use him as a means to accomplish her goal, becoming his queen.

Much time later, after Drangleic was ravaged due to both the war with the Giants and the undead curse, which all of Vendrick’s and Aldia’s plans to cure were in vain, Vendrick found out about Nashandra's plan: to use the throne to claim the First Flame for herself. Vendrick reacted quickly and sent the Throne Watcher and the Throne Defender to guard the throne. He then fled to the Undead Crypt, where he eventually went Hollow, to keep his ring and soul from the wrong hands. He did all this in an attempt to stop Nashandra.

title: Drangleic
snippet: drangleic_s_curses : At a certain point Nashandra, a woman of exceptional beauty, arrived in Drangleic from a foreign country, and entered Vendrick's good graces, becoming his consort. The woman warned the king of a country of Giants beyond the Northern Sea, creatures that possessed souls of immense power and that apparently presented an impending threat to his kingdom. Vendrick was himself interested in the strength of the Giants, which he coveted as a means to step closer to fire, to end the curse of Undeath. The king was seduced by Nashandra's words, and followed her advice to gather an army and cross the Northern Sea, in an effort to subjugate the Giants and claim their souls for himself. When Vendrick landed on the realm of the Giants, a brutal war ensued, where he slaughtered, pillaged and conducted every act of barbarism with Nashandra at his side. title: Drangleic
snippet: Thanks to this discovery Vendrick became the monarch who came closest to becoming a true "King" and turning his wants into reality. He had access to the primordial Flame whose power could decide the fate of the world, either by linking it to prolong the state of the world or refusing this fate and leading the world to darkness as a Dark Lord. Vendrick, however, never made either decision and continued to reign over Drangleic. Both he and his brother were not convinced by the two possible choices and, anchored to the illusion of the form that life had during the Age of Fire, they looked for a way to maintain it, searching for a way to free humans from the curse of Undeath and breaking the seal of fire that imprisoned them. As he deepened his knowledge of souls and curses, Vendrick effectively reigned over Drangleic, protecting the country from any external threats. Nashandra helped bring peace to the kingdom, a peace so profound that it reminded humans of the Dark from which they came.

title: Nashandra
snippet: Left without a king and with no means to claim the Throne of Want, Nashandra’s plans were stalled until the arrival of the Bearer of the Curse, an undead powerful enough to defeat the Four Old Ones and gain access to Drangleic Castle. Nashandra manipulated the Bearer of the Curse into opening the way to the Throne of Want by aiding them in seizing the Throne of Want. She directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Undead Crypt, suggesting that they put an end to the now-hollowed King Vendrick and claim his ring. She then directs the Bearer of the Curse to journey to Aldia's Keep to acquire the Ashen Mist Heart, and warns them that the Ancient Dragon there is no more than a prop and a false deity. At last, she directs the Bearer of the Curse toward the Forest of Fallen Giants to visit the memories of the Giants and obtain the last key to the Throne: the Giant's Kinship.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Nashandra began her life as a small fragment of Manus, Father of the Abyss. When Manus was defeated, he was reborn as many fragments varying in sizes. Nashandra was the incarnation of her "father's" want, and thus began desiring what she did not have: power.

Nashandra travelled to the land of Drangleic, and set her sights on its powerful ruler, King Vendrick. Deciding to seduce Vendrick, Nashandra assumed a human form of unparalleled beauty and warned him of a supposed looming threat beyond the sea: the Giants. She convinced him to invade the land of the giants to claim their power, which Vendrick did successfully. Vendrick then made Nashandra his queen, and under their leadership, Drangleic entered into a Dark-like peace. The rulership of Drangleic however, was not enough to quell Nashandra’s want, and she desired an even greater power: the First Flame, which she intended to claim for herself by using Vendrick and the Throne of Want.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Centuries after the end of Vendrick's reign, Drangleic would be known in Lothric as "Drang", the land of the legend of the Linking of the Fire. Vendrick's name has been lost to history, who is remembered only as the "Old King of Want", an ancient ruler that was cursed by an all-consuming thirst, making him no king at all in the end. The Dragonriders of his royal guard and their immense strength are also properly remembered. A group of soldiers, who proclaimed themselves descendants of Drangleic and wore the geisteel armor made by the blacksmith of Vendrick's Castle, abandoned the region and became sellswords. Known as Drang Knights, they scattered across the lands and quickly became known for shieldless, aggressive fighting tactics that utilized twinspears and hammers, striking fear into the hearts of their enemies.

The stalwart soldiers of Vendrick did not abandon their posts even as they became hollows, guarding their stations without relent. Distinguished soldiers were rewarded with magical rings that empowered them to carry more equipment, as proof of their meritorious deeds. Velstadt and Raime, two distinguished knights, became the left and right arms of Vendrick. Raime was enticed by the strength of his lord and acknowledged him as a father figure, while Velstadt was lured into Drangleic from a faraway home and devoted himself in life and death to his lord, eventually forgetting why he even came to the realm. Velstadt also became the leader of the elite

 trivia : According to the *Dark Souls II: Design Works* interview, Nashandra's design was inspired by Gravelord Nito's, and in the early versions of the story she was not meant to be the Final Boss, instead she had a role closer to Nito's from the first game. However, it is clarified that the two characters aren't directly linked.
**Her design also serves to link well with *Dark Souls II's* theme of "deep curse" - the world's curse of Undeath and the grim fate of the Undead to be chosen to perform an impossible task - that director Yu Tanimura wanted to draw out in the game.
In the Memory of the King, Vendrick refers to her under the shortened name "Shandra", likely his nickname for her.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - lead 
 lead : **Nashandra** or **Queen Nashandra** is a boss and the main antagonist of *Dark Souls II*. She is fought at the end of the Throne of Want area, only after the player has obtained the Giant's Kinship; if the Throne Watcher and Defender have not already been defeated, Nashandra's boss fight will trigger automatically after theirs.

Although she is the final boss of the base game, the *Scholar of the First Sin* expansion added Aldia as a potential "true" final boss, whose battle triggers after Nashandra's if conditions are met. Prior to her boss fight, she appears as a special character in human form atop Drangleic Castle, where she can be talked to from afar.

title: Drangleic
snippet: Initially the king took over the existing structures that had helped contain the curse under previous countries such as the Lost Bastille and the No-man's Wharf, using the golems and creatures already present such as the Flexile Sentries and the Ruin Sentinels as jailers. title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Battles waged endlessly between Vendrick's forces and the Giants, and much of Drangleic's citizens fled the kingdom to escape the conflict. Ultimately, the Giants were defeated by an unnamed hero. In the aftermath, much of Drangleic had been reduced to rubble, and visitors to the kingdom were rare. Many Giants were killed in the conflict, and their corpses eventually grew into large trees that sprawled across the once prosperous kingdom. The last known Giant to have survived the conflict was terribly wounded and kept prisoner in a cavern beneath the Forest of Fallen Giants. It was later discovered another two Giants survived the war, but remained hidden in a cavern in Black Gulch.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: While the Giants invasion was largely stopped, their souls remained powerful. King Vendrick's elder brother, Lord Aldia, kept Giants in his manor and performed experiments on them in an attempt to recreate a dragon. The outcome of Lord Aldia's experiments is unknown, but oddly when the Ancient Dragon roosting at the summit of Aldia's realm was slain, the soul of a Giant was found in its remains. Legend holds that the Giants' resentment of King Vendrick was possibly emboldened in death. This was proven true when the Bearer of the Curse fought the hollowed remains of Vendrick. With the souls of several Giants in the Bearer's possession, Vendrick was significantly weakened and subsequently defeated.

snippet: While Drangleic prospered under Vendrick, the king's older brother Aldia never took an interest in the political affairs of the kingdom he had helped found, preferring to remain in his mansion and dedicating himself to the research of the truths of the world. He earned the title of "holy knight" and was feared for his "demonic power" by his enemies. However, some cleric knights of Lindelt defected to escape their country's authoritarian rule. Even the name has some thematic and etymological connection to Seath, as Shira resembles the Japanese word for "white", written as "**白**" and pronounced "*shiro*", a kanji that makes up part of the Duke's title of "White Dragon", written as "**白竜**". It doesn't stop there, though, as the name also shares an impressive connection with Priscilla's, as Shira's Japanese name "**シラ**" is part of the Crossbreed's Japanese name "**プリシラ**". Priscilla's connections to Seath come from her stark white coloration and her nature as a half-dragon, as crossbreeds were something the old Paledrake was highly interested in. This would make the two half-sisters, but not full ones, as Priscilla is stated to have been born of adultery, meaning they'd have two distinct mothers.

 trivia : Due to what was observed from Artorias, the phrase "falling into the Abyss" does not actually constitute entering it, but rather the near infinite and unconscious darkness of it seeking out lifeforms.
**This likely means that Wolnir was very much alive when he fell, which explains how he was able to teach grave wardens his pyromancy, though what exactly it really was that actually caused his death is uncertain.

title: Emerald Herald
snippet:
Emerald Herald -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : The Emerald Herald's real name is Shanalotte, a name given to her by the dragons. Born of dragons but contrived by men, she was created specifically to break the undead curse, but her creators failed and she did not come out as intended. Despite this, she guides undead towards the Throne of Want, waiting for a powerful undead that might defeat the Four Old Ones, succeed Vendrick and end the undead curse.

title: Bone Scythe
snippet:
Bone Scythe -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : Scythe forged from the soul of the Covetous Demon.

The curved spine of the Covetous Demon is as hard as rock, and rather than slicing through flesh, this weapon seems to grind it apart.

That thing that ended up a monstrous fiend, what was it to begin with, and why did it never leave the queen? Perhaps it was entranced by some perversion of love.

title: Giant Lord
snippet:
Giant Lord -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : The Giant Lord is the king of all Giants. After his kingdom was invaded by King Vendrick, who was under the influence of Nashandra, the Giant Lord invaded Drangleic to avenge his losses, and to retrieve the prize that Vendrick stole from him. Possessing a will of iron, the giants laid siege to Drangleic in a war that lasted for generations, and laid waste to the once proud kingdom. Eventually the Giant Lord was defeated by an unknown hero, and the giants retreated, crossing the sea to return home. The Giant Lord himself, broken and beaten, was dragged beneath the fort where he fell, and imprisoned there.

title: Four Knights of Gwyn
snippet:
Four Knights of Gwyn -  Dark Souls - character - rings 
 rings : Each of the Four Knights was gifted a unique ring imbued with special powers. The Chosen Undead can find them scattered throughout Lordran, and their item descriptions give minor insight into who the knights were and what they did.

title: Company Captain Yorshka
snippet: At some point, after Gwyndolin had become the "Chief Deity" of the Anor Londo clan, Yorshka reached Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, the city her brother had built on the ruins of Anor Londo to house the Irithyllians, hybrids between the race of the gods of Anor Londo and humans. Here she was welcomed by Gwyndolin who formed a relationship of deep affection with his newfound sister, giving her a sacred chime and even the name Yorshka. Eventually a church was built in her name inside Irithyll—exactly where the Painted World of Ariamis was once kept— in which she was venerated as a goddess by the humans who worked in the city.

title: Dark Soul
snippet: Near the end of the Age of Fire, a slave knight called Gael traveled to the Ringed City, seeking the Pygmy Lords to gain their blood. The blood of the Dark Soul was intended to be used to paint a new Painted World, but to Gael's shock, Filianore's spell was broken and the Pygmy Lords were aged to the point that their blood did not flow, for it was dried in their veins. Even though he knew he had not the strength to survive bearing it, Gael slew the Pygmy Lords and drank from their wounds, absorbing the Dark Soul into himself. It imbued him with a dark miasma and warped his mind, but in the end he was successful, slain by the Ashen One to extract the soul's blood. The current state of the Dark Soul is unknown, but given the eternal nature of Lord Souls, it is unlikely that it was truly destroyed.

title: Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin
snippet:
Aldia, Scholar of the First Sin -  Dark Souls II - boss - locations 
 locations : #He is first encountered in the final primal bonfire room that remains unlit. If all bonfires have been lit prior to downloading the patch, he will automatically appear in the Black Gulch primal bonfire room, after The Rotten.
#Upon speaking to the player at the primal bonfire, Aldia will proceed to the first bonfire in the Undead Crypt.
#After exhausting his dialogue in the Undead Crypt, Aldia can be found in the Dragon Shrine bonfire room, at a significantly reduced size compared to the first bonfire.
#Finally, after completing the dialogue in Dragon Shrine, Aldia will appear as a boss in the Throne of Want in Drangleic Castle after killing Nashandra, but only if Vendrick is killed before Nashandra. The game can be completed without fighting Aldia here, if Nashandra is killed before Vendrick is.

title: Hollow Mage
snippet:
Hollow Mage -  Dark Souls II - enemy - lore 
 lore : These mages are related to the Necromancers. As described by their Set, the ones in this group that did not practice necromancy were all male. While these individuals were generally sorcerers, they carry Skeptic's Spice and Rouge Water, thus implying that either they belonged to a religious group, or that they also used some Miracles.

While the women went under the service of the Iron King, it's unknown what these sorcerers did or where they went.

Centuries later, these sorcerers would reach Tseldora (whether before or after the city was ruined by the spiders is unknown)

snippet:

 throne_of_want : Below Drangleic Castle, the Throne of Want awaits. Here the Emerald Herald will meet the Bearer of the Curse one final time, declaring her journey completed. She warns that if the Bearer of the Curse proceeds, Nashandra, knowing the Bearer of the Curse will link the fire, and coveting the power of the First Flame and the Great Soul, will come for them. She urges the Bearer of the Curse to put an end to Nashandra.

After defeating the Throne Watcher and Defender, the Bearer of the Curse will be greeted by Nashandra, now in her true form, as a child of Manus, Father of the Abyss. The Bearer of the Curse defeats Nashandra.

title: Burnt Ivory King
snippet: Once all of the Knights are dead, the Burnt Ivory King will appear from a massive portal that rises at the end of the arena. Note that the player will have a good amount of time between when the Knights are killed and when the King appears. If the player did not rescue at least two other Knights of Eleum Loyce, two of the portals will remain open and spawning Knights during the fight with the king, possibly proving to be a fatal distraction.

title: Guardian Dragon
snippet:
Guardian Dragon -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : The "Guardian Dragon" is a wyvern that guards the way to Dragon Aerie. Thanks to his experiments and magic, Aldia learned how to control wyverns, commanding this subject to act as a guardian and closing it inside a improvised cage located between his Keep and the Aerie.

In the ruins of Heide, another "Guardian Dragon" can be found guarding the Cathedral of Blue. It is possible that it is the mount of the Dragonrider who resides nearby in Heide, the elite knights of Vendrick who once rode earth dragons and that would mount wyverns after Aldia learned to control them.

title: Way of Blue (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Way of Blue (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Given by Emma, High Priestess of Lothric Castle at the end of the High Wall of Lothric, along with the Small Lothric Banner.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Giant (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - enemy - giant_memories 
 giant_memories : Once the Ashen Mist Heart has been obtained, it can be used to interact with the corpses of three fallen Giants who fought in the war against Vendrick. The heart grants access to the memories of Jeigh, Orro and Vammar. In these memories, the player can witness various battles that took place between the Giants and Vendrick's army. According to Sweet Shalquoir, the Giants savour their memories of glory on the battlefield.

title: Dragonslayer Armour
snippet: The army of Lothric successfully hunted down the wyverns in their region; moreover, by observing how their god commanded such creatures, they even learned how to tame and ride them, and wyverns became a symbol of Lothric alongside its knights. With the wyverns dead or domesticated, the dragonslayers were rendered obsolete, and their armour was retired in favor of lighter, more conventional knight armor. The armour of an ancient Dragonslayer, however, remained in the barracks of the Lothric army, on the bridge between the Altar of Sunlight and the Grand Archives, a monument to the legendary past of Lothric knights.

title: Path of the Dragon
snippet:
Path of the Dragon -  Dark Souls - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : Talk to the Stone Dragon in Ash Lake. To access Ash Lake, travel from Blighttown to The Great Hollow and get to its very bottom; upon arriving there, follow the path along the beach to its end.

title: Heide's Tower of Flame
snippet: founders had inherited a strong relationship with the knowledge of the city of the gods. Another element that proves the connection between Heide and Anor Londo is the fact that the Cathedral of Blue is defended by an Old Dragonslayer, whose appearance and artifacts are identical to that of the knights who served Dragon Slayer Ornstein, thus implying that some of them or knowledge of their heritage had come to the city of Drangleic.

title: Olenford
snippet: He was certainly a key figure at that time, and may have been one of the founders of the Melfian Magic Academy due to his importance to the sorcerers of Melfia. Yet Olenford was seemingly unsatisfied with his current standing, instead seeking knowledge that surpassed that of mere men. This search would lead him to the Undead Crypt, a treasure trove of ancient wisdom kept safe by the Fenito, and it is there that he did away with his humanity. What that entails is a mystery, but all that remains now is his staff, stored away in that very crypt.

 hornet_ring : Engraved with a hornet, the Hornet Ring belonged to Lord's Blade Ciaran. Increasing the power of critical attacks, it allows its wearer to lay waste to their foes much like how Ciaran did to Lord Gwyn's enemies.

title: Ring of Blind Ghosts
snippet:
Ring of Blind Ghosts -  Dark Souls - ring - overview 
 overview : As the description states, the Ring of Blind Ghosts was intended to prevent the wearer from being attacked by Ghosts and Banshees in the New Londo Ruins. It was also connected to Ingward, however, as it was removed from the game before release, it is unknown how the player would have obtained it normally.

title: Astora
snippet: At some point Astora was assaulted by a dark beast, bearing an evil eye that absorbed the vitality of its victims, that ravaged the country until the land was almost destroyed. However this horrid spirit was eventually defeated by one of the noblest knights. Although it was killed, the strength of the creature did not waver and its spirit was captured into a magic ring with its eye that kept its life-absorbing power.

title: Farron Coal
snippet:
Farron Coal -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : Found in the Road of Sacrifices on what once was the eastern access to the keep. The area can be reached by following the eastern shore of the marsh, fighting a couple of Lycanthropes along the way. The coal can be found at the end of a blocked passageway, guarded by a Black Knight.

title: Heide's Tower of Flame
snippet: In Heide would also have originated the Way of Blue, which was not a developed religion but a humble prayer that spread naturally among those seeking help, but which eventually grew to the point that a huge Cathedral of Blue was built in the heart of the city. To fill the same role played by the Blades of the Darkmoon, the Blue Sentinels would be formed, a group that descended directly from the original Blades of the Darkmoon.They were tasked with defending the apostles of Blue from evil spirits by traveling between space and time thanks to the Cracked Blue Eye Orbs. The victorious knights would be rewarded with miracles from the ancient gods of Anor Londo like Wrath of the Gods and Bountiful Sunlight that had been lost or jealously guarded elsewhere in Drangleic, again implying that Heide's founders had inherited a strong relationship with the knowledge of the city of the gods. title: Ring of Displacement
snippet:
Ring of Displacement -  Dark Souls - ring - overview 
 overview : As the description states, the Ring of Displacement was intended to prevent the wearer from taking damage. However, in order to balance this, it had a fixed chance of breaking whilst it was worn. As it was removed from the game before release, it is unknown how the player would have obtained it normally.

title: Bearer of the Curse
snippet:
Bearer of the Curse -  Dark Souls II - character - undead_crypt 
 undead_crypt : After traveling through the Shrine of Amana, the Bearer of the Curse will come upon the Undead Crypt, a place that has stood since the dawn of time, and where men and gods alike have been interred. Here, Vendrick came along with his loyal knights and his right hand, Velstadt, the Royal Aegis. Many servants of Vendrick have come to find the King, only to meet their end at the hands of the Royal Aegis and the King's knights.

Upon descending from the elevator, the Bearer of the Curse will stumble upon the Scholar once more if met at the last primal bonfire. The Scholar will ask the Bearer if they still desire peace, if answered yes, he will tell them that Vendrick is here and not far off. He will state that the Bearer was neither born with greatness nor granted it by the fates, before once again disappearing into the flames.

title: Shield of Want
snippet:
Shield of Want -  Dark Souls III - weapon - trivia

title: Crossbreed Priscilla
snippet:
***Priscilla would later become the Lady of said world, perhaps inheriting the title from the would-be original owner, Velka.
***Even if Velka was not herself involved in the creation of the Painting, the tendency of Velka's artifacts and cultists to end up in the Painted World, which welcomed those without a place in the realm of Gods, hints towards some correlation between Velka and Priscilla.

 dark_souls_iii : In the times and region of Lothric, despite the many centuries that passed, Rendal's ring that offered great physical protection was passed around and it was said that he was lined with steel on the inside, such that even the talons of mighty dragons did him little harm, thus keeping the last trace of Balder's existence until the last days of the Fire.

title: Zullie the Witch
snippet:
Zullie the Witch -  Dark Souls III - character - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Tales and songs of Alva's exploits and travels still persist in the era of Lothric, and with him the figures of Zullie and Serreta. Sadly, those stories tend to end in tragedy.

It can be surmised that Zullie's end was also quite tragic, as a corpse with the entirety of her set can be found in the Ringed City, guarded by the very knight that had given her life meaning long ago. Yet the witch cannot simply rest either, seeing as her spirit is summoned by the Judicator Giants who preside over the legendary city. Since her body lay abandoned unceremoniously in a corner of the city, it's unlikely that she befriended the wizened beings the way Silver Knight Ledo did long ago, so she was probably forced into the role like the ancient company of knights that came before her, as punishment for her trespass.

title: Dreamchaser's Ashes
snippet:
Dreamchaser's Ashes -  Dark Souls III - item - trivia 
 trivia : The icon shows an ashen hand that is clutching what appears to be the Pendant from *Dark Souls*, an item that had no practical use in the game.
**When the Shrine Handmaid is given these ashes, she will ask the Ashen One where they found them. Upon telling her, she will comment how they must have belonged to "one most foolish indeed", perhaps hinting at players trying to figure out the hidden use, which did not actually exist, for the Pendant after Hidetaka Miyazaki, director of *Dark Souls* and *Dark Souls III*, said he'd either choose the Pendant or nothing as his starting gift.

title: Chime of Want
snippet:
Chime of Want -  Dark Souls II - weapon - description 
 description : Sacred chime created from the soul of Nashandra. Greatly amplifies spells.

The old one of the Abyss was reborn in death, split into miniscule fragments, and spread across the land.
The tiniest of these pieces, precisely due to its size, was the first to restore its form.

title: The Pursuer
snippet:
The Pursuer -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : The Pursuers are large hulking knights who hunt down those who bear the undead curse, possibly to atone for past sins committed. Wielding an ultra greatsword renowned for being one of the mightiest of its design, the Pursuers will relentlessly stalk its target until slain. It is unknown if the Pursuers served under King Vendrick, as did many other knights, or if they acted off of their own accord.

title: Fume Knight
snippet:
Fume Knight -  Dark Souls II - boss - lore 
 lore : Raime was one of Drangleic's most distinguished knights. He used his favorite bird, the black raven, as his sigil. He was considered by Vendrick as his left arm and was one of his most trusted advisors along with Velstadt. However, he eventually clashed with Velstadt and was deemed a traitor by Vendrick.

title: Curse (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Curse (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - notes 
 notes : During the fight with Nashandra, she will cast four dark orbs that surround her and curse the player, while also draining their health; achieving curse immunity will not negate the health drain.
If the player gathers all three crowns from *The Lost Crowns* DLCs as well as the King's Crown, and returns to the Undead Crypt and uses the Ashen Mist Heart to speak to Vendrick, they are awarded Vendrick's Blessing, granting immunity to Curse, and won't hollow upon death as long as they are wearing the King's Crown, Crown of the Sunken King, Crown of the Old Iron King, or Crown of the Ivory King.

title: Company of Champions
snippet:
Company of Champions -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - how_to_join 
 how_to_join : The player can join this covenant as soon as they arrive to Majula. Going between the houses of Lenigrast and Shalquoir, a ledge extending from the cliffside can be found which leads to the Victor's Stone. Upon interacting with the stone, the player must confirm multiple times that they are certain about joining the covenant, and doing so will have them recieve the Champion's Tablet.

title: Ending (Dark Souls II)
snippet:
Ending (Dark Souls II) -  Dark Souls II - mechanic - leave_the_throne 
 leave_the_throne : Available only to those with the *Scholar of the First Sin* version or any patch newer than 1.10 for the original *Dark Souls II*.

This ending only becomes available after the player has defeated Vendrick in the Undead Crypt and after having spoken to Aldia at every bonfire he spawns at throughout the game. Upon defeating Nashandra, Aldia will fight the player as an additional final boss. Upon defeating Aldia, both endings are available to the player, and choosing to exit the Throne of Want through the fog wall will result in this ending.

In this ending, the Bearer of the Curse rejects the throne, and bitterly walks away, seemingly to seek another, more permanent way to end the curse.

Long ago, an Undead declared a fight. A fight to celebrate their undeath, and so to preserve what remained of their souls. So it was that the Undead Matches were born. The merit of an Undead is measured in deaths. Could there be a greater gift for such a creature, than a fight that has no end?

snippet:
The Nameless King -  Dark Souls III - boss - dark_souls_iii 
 dark_souls_iii : Over the centuries, the Nameless King would continue to lead a warrior's life and take part in countless battles, fighting alongside his stormdrake with whom he forged a relationship of profound camaraderie, coming to consider him as a comrade in arms as was an ancient custom among soldiers of the gods.

title: Jugo
snippet:
Also in Jugo was a particular group made up mostly of women known as the Desert Sorceresses. These were skilled pyromancers who utilized "flame fans" rather than basic pyromancy flames, suggesting an ability to exploit their country's arid climate to generate fire spells through unconventional sorcery catalysts. They were known for their thin clothing permeated with magic whose revealing nature effectively served as a means to distract weak-willed enemies, helping the sorceresses even enthrall them into their service. At some point after the fall of Vendrick's kingdom, a group of these sorceresses from Jugo moved into Drangleic and settled into the domain of Queen Mytha near the Earthen Peak and Harvest Valley.

A descendant of the Desert Sorceresses of Earthen Peak, Zoey, survived into the end of the Age of Fire. Unlike her predecessors, Zoey did not use her beauty to poison others, instead becoming a queen of sorts to the feeble ones.

title: Oscar, Knight of Astora
snippet:
Oscar, Knight of Astora -  Dark Souls - character - lore 
 lore : Oscar was likely a high-ranking knight from Astora, who was determined to seek out Lordran once he turned undead. Exactly how he ended up in the Undead Asylum and why he rescues the player is unknown, though it is implied that he was intentionally releasing undead from the Asylum in hopes that at least one would ring the Bells of Awakening.

There is a hole in the ceiling at the location he is first encountered, and since the Asylum Demon first appears descending upon the Chosen Undead to guard the exit from any undead hoping to escape, it can be assumed that Oscar had fought the Asylum Demon on the roof of the Asylum, but wound up crashing down into the squalid dungeon the player encounters him in.

It is implied that the ensuing despair he felt at being unable to even overcome his first obstacle as an undead is what turned him Hollow.

title: High Wall of Lothric
snippet:
High Wall of Lothric -  Dark Souls III - location - trivia 
 trivia : In the early demos, the High Wall of Lothric was named the "Wall of Lodeleth".
The building of the Grand Archives, when viewed from the High Wall, was radically altered between the early demos and the final game. It was much smaller in the demos and the two bridges were longer.
There is a dead Outrider Knight in the cell where the Darkwraith is found.

title: Gravelord Nito
snippet: What was once an all-concealing cloak looking like black fur or feather, apparently conjured at will, is reduced to a tattered hairlike cloak. When dormant, Nito did not seem to wear it until after generating a glowing fume of lavender-white power, likely the "miasma of death" he is known for. His left hand is natural, his right is equipped with a triple bone forearm, which terminates in a sharpened bone blade covered with his miasma.

title: Gordin, Wandering Knight of Forossa
snippet:
Gordin, Wandering Knight of Forossa -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Gordin was a knight from the belligerent kingdom of Forossa. He was known for having inherited the Majestic Greatsword, a unique blade of unknown origin, and was the last man to wield it before he perished and the sword was lost. Just like every other swordsman who was in the possession of the greatsword, Gordin was left-handed.

The Majestic Greatsword can still be retrived, stored in the dangerous Brume Tower. Perhaps it's the place where Gordin met his end.

title: Ocelotte
snippet:
Ocelotte -  Dark Souls III - character - trivia 
 trivia : Cut content from *Dark Souls III* includes an unused audio file with what appears to be the sound of a crying baby being murdered. This file was probably intended to be used in Oceiros's boss fight during the transition between the first and the second phase, Ocelotte's last cry when Oceiros disposes of his son.
In the alpha stages of game development, Ocelotte had a static character model made to be carried by Ocerios the Consumed King, depicting an overlarge malformed baby. The model was cut from the final game for unknown reasons, though it is likely due to Ocerios graphically and savagely murdering him in the second phase of his boss fight.

title: Drangleic
snippet:
Drangleic -  Dark Souls II - location - description 
 description : The region of Drangleic is geographically defined by natural barriers: to the north stretches a vast coastline while the other three sides are surrounded by mountains.

Far in the north of Drangleic, beyond the great sea, there is an unexplored continent where the race of the giants lives. To the east, Drangleic borders with the kingdom of Mirrah while in the distant east the land of Jugo and the ruins of the kingdom of Forossa are located.  characteristics : The Drangleic Shield has the potential to be a reliable shield for those that can wield it effectively, as it boasts a high strength requirement as well as a high amount of weight for a medium shield. Nonetheless, it will still most likely be the first shield with a maxed out physical damage resistance the player will find, and as such, it is a must for anyone who doesn't have one with such characteristics. The shield also boasts very high stability for a medium shield, which makes it very useful for fighting enemies that only deal physical damage and for fighting bosses.

#Kill all the surrounding Humanity Phantoms.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Manus may be named for Mannus, the father of mankind in Germanic mythology. According to the Roman writer Tacitus, the Germanic tribes believed a god *Tuisto* sprang from the ground and had a son, *Mannus*, from whom all humans were descended. Manus is also the Latin word for “hand”, alluding to Manus’s massive left hand.
**However a more accurate translation of "深淵の主マヌス" would be "Manus, Lord of the Abyss".

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - notes 
 notes : The Silver Pendant, although not required, can be of great help as it blocks his magic attacks if used with correct timing.

Great Grey Wolf Sif can help in this battle. Whilst Sif's attacks are not very damaging, the extra summon can keep Manus distracted and give the player time to heal. It is wise to only summon Sif after Manus is below half health, to distract him in his harder phase, making it less likely the player will be targeted by the Dark Orb barrage attack.

Sif's summon sign is *inside* the Manus's arena, directly to the left of where the player spawns. As a result, Sif can only be summoned *during* the fight. Thankfully, Sif is summoned instantly after touching the sign, without the usual white phantom-summoning animation. Since it is summoned during the fight it does not increase Manus' Hp.

He wields a staff in his right hand to attack and to cast dark sorceries, while his larger, furry left arm, capable of extending to reach enemies, is complete with a hand laden with teeth inside the palm.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: Manus at one point kidnapped Princess Dusk of Oolacile—possibly after her rescue from a Golden Crystal Golem—and imprisoned her deep within the Chasm of the Abyss. In the meantime, his prized pendant came under the possession of Seath the Scaleless and then a Chosen Undead in the future; Manus, driven by his unrelenting search for his pendant, snatched the Undead from the future and brought them into the old Oolacile. There, the Chosen Undead put down the corrupted Knight Artorias and journeyed within the Chasm of the Abyss, where they finally defeated Manus and put him to rest. While Dusk was rescued in the process, she was driven by Elizabeth into thinking that she was saved by Artorias, preserving the legacy of the Wolf Knight. Nevertheless, Dusk came to recognize the Chosen Undead's similarity to the fabled knight, and developed doubts of her own as to her true savior.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: Manus was a sorcerer of Oolacile, and after he died, his body was buried in the caverns beneath the city. 200 to 300 years prior to the journey of the Chosen Undead, the Primordial Serpent Kaathe arrived in Oolacile, in search of a potential Dark Lord following the flooding of New Londo. He manipulated the country to upturn the grave of the primordial man, Manus, buried beneath the dungeons of their city and resurrect him. Manus awakened to find his pendant missing, and was eventually driven into a beastly frenzy as his Dark Soul went wild, transforming him into the "Father of the Abyss".

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
If the player wishes to face Manus conventionally, it is advisable to equip stamina-boosting items that such as the Cloranthy Ring, as well as a high-Stability shield that blocks physical damage. Only attack Manus after he finishes his jumping smash or frenzy combo, lest you be caught in the middle of his strikes.

Manus will start using his magic attacks at around 50% health. Use the Silver Pendant to deflect them, as they are difficult to dodge.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet:
Manus, Father of the Abyss -  Dark Souls - boss - dark_souls_ii 
 dark_souls_ii : Although he was killed, the Dark Soul of Manus was so large and powerful that he was reborn in death, and his soul split into miniscule fragments that retained some will. These pieces began to coalesce once again by absorbing other humanities, becoming the incarnations of different emotions of Manus and then human in shape, with their own self-awareness: Elana was the embodiment of Manus' wrath, Alsanna of his fear, Nadalia of his solitude and Nashandra, the tiniest fragment of Manus, the embodiment of his want. These new entities had some recollection of their father and his dark powers and when the Abyss that they called home was dissipated they scattered across the land. To sustain themselves and seek power, they reached Drangleic where in one way or another they came into contact with the holders of magnificent souls, drawn to their awesome strength.

title: Manus, Father of the Abyss
snippet: As the Abyss spread across the land of Oolacile, Knight Artorias arrived to halt its advance and confront Manus, as the Knight of Gwyn already had experience with fighting the Abyss and its creatures after the events of New Londo and his hunt for the Darkwraiths, and possessed a Silver Pendant that protected him from the Dark. However, Artorias's pendant was stolen by Oolacile's inhabitants and hidden behind an illusory wall, depriving Artorias of protection against Manus's dark sorceries. Together with his trusted companion Sif, Artorias faced Manus but his strength proved insufficient to defeat him, and he succumbed to the Abyss. Injured in the battle, Artorias used his Cleansing Greatshield to form a magic barrier that protected Sif from the Dark. Now corrupted to his soul by the Abyss and with his armor corroded, Artorias was left to fight alone and hold back the treacherous citizens of Oolacile.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
Nashandra -  Dark Souls II - boss - attacks 
 attacks : ***Curse Fountains**: Summons several white fountains that build up your curse meter. They can be destroyed by a single strike or by a roll.
***Laser Beam**: Her hand fills with darkness and fires a beam at the player. Can be either an easily dodged vertical, or a sweeping shot much like the Duke's Dear Freja. (Can be dodged by rolling backwards; Just be wary of the holes in the arena.)
***Dark Explosion**: Her hand fills with darkness and she brings it closer to her chest. Once her whole body begins to emanate darkness, she releases an area of effect dark attack, similar to Wrath of the Gods.
***Overhead Strike**: Performs an overhead attack with her scythe. Easily dodged.
***Swings**: Swings her scythe twice in a row.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
All of her attacks inflict Curse Build-up.

For melee characters it is also possible to equip light armor and dodge her attacks, ignoring the Curse buildup and only healing when your health starts draining. Also a good method for melee users is to wait at a distance for her to come towards the player, baiting her away from the four curse fountains. The curse fountains can be broken, stopping the curse buildup and health drain.

Summoning help will make the fight easier, even if it's only the two characters Vengarl of Forossa and Benhart of Jugo, as they will draw attention, leaving you with a good amount of room to deal damage and heal as needed.

An effective strategy if one has pyromancies is to stay far away until she fires her vertical "laser", then simply lobbing flame attacks at her.

title: Nashandra
snippet:
**Dark Magic**: She will either fire a beam that starts on the floor close to her and emits outward from the floor vertically, which can easily be avoided by strafing, or execute a small area of effect attack similar to Wrath of the Gods. If she begins casting and her body is *not* being covered in dark energy, then she will use the beam; otherwise, it is the area-of-effect attack and you must back away. If you look closely, you will also notice that her hand movement is different for each attack (she draws her hand close to her chest when using Wrath of the Gods). She also has another type of beam which sweeps horizontally, so be aware of the direction of the beams as these beams are usually fatal when combined with the health drain.

All of her attacks inflict Curse Build-up.

title: Raulmond, Knight of Drangleic
snippet:
Raulmond, Knight of Drangleic -  Dark Souls II - character - theories 
 theories : It's possible that Raulmond is related to Captain Drummond, a warrior of Drangleic whose family has been defending the fort for generations, something Raulmond had done in the past too, until his death. The knight could have been Drummond's father or even grandfather, as both had fought the invading Giants according to the current captain, and might have died during the struggle. The names of the two soldiers are also remarkably similar, which would make a lot of sense if they were related in some way.

title: Raulmond, Knight of Drangleic
snippet:
Raulmond, Knight of Drangleic -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Raulmond was a knight who served King Vendrick in his time, acting as a guardian of his fort until his own demise. He was known for cershing rings that bore the protection of dragons throughout all of his life and service to Drangleic. He might have been an exceptional champion, however, as the first of his rings is the second highest reward of the Company of Champions covenant, a group of brave warriors based in Majula who scoff at danger and seek greater challenges, their names engraved to commemorate their deeds.
